title: A Practical Guide to Efficient AI: Shelby Heinecke

primary.label: AI Platforms & Developer Tooling
primary.rationale: The talk's primary focus is post-training quantization, inference efficiency, and quantization frameworks for serving models in production and constrained environments. The efficiency techniques are cross-domain, applicable to cloud, on-prem, and mobile/edge deployment without being specific to any application vertical. The talk centers on deploying models efficiently via quantization and evaluating quantized models before deployment. Assumes familiarity with LLMs and deployment concepts but remains practical rather than deeply theoretical. Recorded conference presentation at the AI Engineer World's Fair. summary: Shelby Heinecke presents a practical guide to efficient AI at the AI Engineer World's Fair. She leads an AI research team at Salesforce that ships LLM solutions and has released 15+ research papers and 6+ open source repos. Salesforce has deployed AI for 10 years, accumulating 300+ AI patents and 227+ research papers, serving Fortune 500 scale customers. She frames efficiency as the key bridge between demos and productionized AI, noting models are deployed in constrained environments: cloud (paying for resource consumption), on-prem (restricted GPUs), and increasingly small devices like iPhones. She identifies five orthogonal dimensions of efficiency: (1) efficient architecture selection (small models, mixture of experts, efficient attention), (2) efficient pre-training (mixed precision training, scaling methods), (3) efficient fine-tuning (LoRA, QLoRA), (4) efficient inference (post-training quantization, speculative decoding), and (5) prompting (concise prompts, template formatting, prompt compression). She dives deep into small LLMs (≤13B parameters), highlighting Phi-3 (3.8B, outperforms a 7B model), MobileLLM (350M, on par with 7B after fine-tuning), and Octopus (2B fine-tuned Gemma, outperforms GPT-4 and Llama 7B on Android function calling). The talk then covers post-training quantization in depth: reducing weight precision from 32/16-bit floats to 8-bit or 4-bit, yielding massive reductions in disk space, memory, CPU/GPU usage, and improved latency (time to first token). Quantization generally has negligible effects on performance at 4-bit, but performance drops at 3-bit, so evaluating quantized models before deployment is critical. She recommends frameworks like llama.cpp (supporting 16-bit down to 1.5-bit quantization, with many pre-quantized models available on HuggingFace) and ONNX Runtime (8-bit quantization, cross-language compatibility). Her team recently released Mobile AI Bench, an open-source framework for rigorously evaluating quantized models across text tasks, trust and safety, and vision-language tasks, including an iOS app that measures latency and hardware usage such as battery drainage.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and Context
sections.summary: Shelby introduces herself, her AI research team at Salesforce, and the gap between demos and productionized AI, framing efficiency as the key bridge.

sections.title: Salesforce AI Background
sections.summary: Overview of Salesforce's 10-year AI deployment history, 300+ patents, 227+ papers, ethical AI councils, and recent LLM product deployments at Fortune 500 scale.

sections.title: Deployment Environments and Constrained Resources
sections.summary: Describes deployment environments — cloud, on-prem with restricted GPUs, and small devices including iPhones — emphasizing that resources are always constrained.

sections.title: Five Dimensions of Efficiency
sections.summary: Introduces five orthogonal efficiency dimensions: architecture selection, pre-training, fine-tuning, inference, and prompting, with specific technique examples for each.

sections.title: Small LLMs: The Power of Efficient Architectures
sections.summary: Defines small LLMs as ≤13B parameters, contrasts with large models like PaLM (540B), and explains benefits: less RAM, less GPU/CPU, faster fine-tuning, low latency, and deployment flexibility across mobile, laptop, and edge.

sections.title: Small Model Examples: Phi-3, MobileLLM, Octopus
sections.summary: Showcases three small models: Phi-3 (3.8B) outperforming a 7B model, MobileLLM (350M) on par with 7B after fine-tuning, and Octopus (2B fine-tuned Gemma) outperforming GPT-4 and Llama 7B on Android tasks. Transitions to quantization topic.

sections.title: Quantization: Concept, Benefits, and Performance
sections.summary: Explains post-training quantization: reducing weight precision from 32/16-bit floats to 8-bit or 4-bit, yielding massive reductions in disk space, memory, CPU/GPU usage, and improved latency (time to first token). Shows Llama model disk space reductions and LMM latency improvements. Demonstrates that 4-bit quantization has negligible performance impact on a vision-language task, but 3-bit causes performance drops, emphasizing the need to evaluate quantized models before deployment.

sections.title: Quantization Frameworks, Mobile AI Bench, and Conclusion
sections.summary: Highlights quantization frameworks: llama.cpp (16-bit down to 1.5-bit, wide adoption, pre-quantized models on HuggingFace) and ONNX Runtime (8-bit, cross-language compatibility). Introduces Mobile AI Bench, an open-source framework from Shelby's team for evaluating quantized models across text, trust/safety, and vision-language tasks, including an iOS app measuring latency and hardware usage like battery drainage. Concludes by reminding the audience of the five dimensions of AI efficiency.

demonstrations: Showed Phi-3 technical report benchmark clip demonstrating it outperforms a well-known 7B model

Showed Llama model disk space reduction with 4-bit quantization (7B, 13B, 70B taking a fraction of original space)
Showed large multimodal model latency improvement (time to first token) with 4-bit quantization vs 16-bit
Showed LMM performance comparison across 16-bit, 8-bit, 4-bit, and 3-bit quantization on a vision-language task
limitations: Five dimensions only scratch the surface of efficiency techniques
Talk covers only two of five dimensions in depth due to limited time
Not many practitioners are doing pre-training due to expense
